pathwayLabel: Out-of-State Examination Pathway — No Coursework or Job-Site-Hour Requirements; 2 Years Holding the Florida License Substitutes for Standard Prerequisites
examName: TSBPE Out-of-State Journeyman Plumber Examination (computer-based + practical) or Master Plumber Examination (computer-based only) — required regardless of the Florida license
steps: Texas TSBPE has no blanket reciprocity agreement with Florida — its only confirmed signed reciprocal agreement is with Louisiana (confirmed directly from tsbpe.texas.gov/louisianareciprocity/); a second reciprocal state, Arkansas, appears in secondary sourcing but has not been independently fetch-confirmed; Florida is not on this list under either version of it.

Texas does offer a real, separate Out-of-State Examination pathway — confirmed by direct text extraction of TSBPE's own 'Out-of-State Examination Application' (revised March 2026) — open to any current Journeyman or Master Plumber license from another state, including Florida.

This pathway requires proof the out-of-state license has been held for at least 2 years. It does NOT require the 8,000-hour job-site experience log or the 48-hour classroom training that Texas's own standard, in-state Journeyman Examination Application demands — the out-of-state license itself substitutes for those prerequisites under this specific application.
Submit a legible copy of the current Florida license, proof of US work authorization, a government-issued photo ID, and complete one-time fingerprinting through IdentoGO.
Pay the non-refundable processing fee: $40 for the Journeyman track, $25 for the Master track.
Pass the required exam: the Journeyman track is computer-based (Pearson VUE) plus a practical hands-on component; the Master track is computer-based only.
A failed exam carries a mandatory waiting period before retesting: 30 days after a first failure, 60 days after a second, 90 days after a third or later failure.
notes: This record supersedes an earlier, less precise characterization drawn from a WebFetch AI-summary of TSBPE's license-types web pages, which described the benefit as a '48-hour training waiver conditioned on holding an out-of-state license' and cited a '1 year for Master with an approved apprenticeship' figure. Direct pdftotext extraction of the two actual, current TSBPE application PDFs (the standard Journeyman Examination Application and the separate Out-of-State Examination Application, both fetched and read in full) shows a cleaner picture: out-of-state Journeyman/Master license holders don't get a conditional waiver bolted onto the standard application — they use an entirely separate application track with its own, simpler requirement set (2 years' prior licensure, no coursework, no job-site-hour log), and the fee is $40 (Journeyman) or $25 (Master), not the assumed-generic figure used elsewhere on this site. The 8,000-hour and 48-hour-classroom requirements described in the standard Journeyman Examination Application do not appear anywhere in the Out-of-State Examination Application and are not applicable to this pathway. Arkansas's status as a second reciprocal state (beyond the directly-confirmed Louisiana) remains WebSearch-sourced only and unconfirmed by direct fetch — flagged rather than silently upgraded, though it does not affect this Florida-specific record.
